title: Serial Founder – a startup game where an LLM plays the investors (Free demo)
author: RefrigeratorMedium41
selftext:
I have been building Serial Founder game alone since July, with Claude Code doing most of the typing. Free demo on Steam, Windows and Mac, under an hour per run. [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5118720/Serial\_Founder/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_campaign=aigamedev](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5118720/Serial_Founder/?utm_source=reddit&utm_campaign=aigamedev)

You type your startup idea in your own words. Then you try to make it a company: find someone to build it, make a first sale, don't run out of money, get a VC fund into a room. In full game, there are scale and exit phases of the game as well.

The tech part I think is interesting here:

Game is using LLM API realtime to make meetings realistic and to support all possible business ideas. However, the LLM never decides anything. It only talks. Every turn of an investor meeting is one structured call to Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite. It rewrites the investor's question and all your answer options to fit your idea. If the model returns something broken or is not available, the written text is shown instead. I tried local models as well, but I did not get them working consistently enough.

The VC investment decision is plain code, an algorithm. Each fund has a ledger of what it needs to know: team, market, traction, moat, unit economics, the ask, each to a certain depth. A fund says yes only if the ledger is covered with no contradictions. So nobody funds you in the first meeting. You leave with homework, and usually with "we love the space, we're just not leading right now".

If a fund catches you contradicting yourself, it gets harder to convince for the rest of the game. So know your numbers. Get caught three times and that fund will never say yes. Before I added that rule, my test bots found that bluffing was faster than honesty (not sure if this is realistic...).

Every run comes from one seed, so the same choices always give the same run. When I change a game number, like a salary or how hard a fund is, a bot plays 12,800 runs before and after, and I compare how often players get funded or go bankrupt. I also test with LLM players that see only the screen as text.

The LLM model calls go through a small relay on Cloudflare Workers, so no API key is in the build. A demo run costs me about 5-8 cents. There is a cap per install and a daily cap. When the money runs out, the game plays on with the written lines.

Tip: take a co-founder early, or half of the town stays locked.

Happy to answer anything, especially about keeping an LLM inside a game's rules
